clue.text: In Bach, a vocal representation of chaos

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A Bach vocal piece that depicts chaos, perhaps the opening of a cantata.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation of' is a link: the answer is the run straddling BacH A VOCal.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc is widespread disorder and destruction, a close synonym for chaos.

clue.text: Issue suppressed by Judge Jeffreys's satellites?

indicators.note: suppressed by means the issue sits underneath in this down entry

parts.note: Judge Jeffreys was the notorious hanging judge, so a hanger
a son is a child, one's issue

explanation.surface: Offspring kept down by the hanging judge's hangers-on.
explanation.walkthrough: George Jeffreys was the seventeenth-century 'hanging judge' of the Bloody Assizes, so a hanger.
explanation.definitionFit: Satellites in the figurative sense are dependants or followers who attach themselves to someone powerful.

clue.text: Considerable length of garment worn by Russian leader

indicators.note: worn by means the garment goes around its wearer, holding it inside

parts.note: a vest is an undergarment

indicators.note: leader asks for the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A large piece of clothing worn by the head of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: A verst is an old Russian unit of distance of about a kilometre, a considerable length.

clue.text: Open country said to produce this wine

indicators.note: said signals that the word for open country is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: champaign is an old word for level open country

explanation.surface: Open countryside is said to make this wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to produce' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is the sparkling wine from the French region of that name.

clue.text: Island rejected by convention, though suitable for occupancy

parts.note: a habit is a custom or established practice, a convention

indicators.note: rejected means the island's name is thrown back, so read from right to left

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: An island turned down by some convention, even though it is fit to live on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the island backwards, and that follows the custom; 'by' and 'though' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitable place is fit to be lived in, suitable for people to occupy.

clue.text: It may leave one with only a bob

definitions.text: It may leave one with only a bob

parts.words: It may leave one with only a bob
parts.note: a bob is a short hairstyle, and also an old shilling, as if a cut left one nearly broke

explanation.definitionFit: A visit to the barber can leave you with a short bob hairstyle.

clue.text: Incompetent player appears to assimilate Beethoven's Ninth

indicators.note: appears to assimilate means the musician takes the letter in

parts.note: a bugler is a player of the bugle

indicators.note: Ninth here means the ninth letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: An inept musician seems to absorb Beethoven's Ninth Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: The ninth letter of BEETHOVEN is N, not the symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungler botches things, an incompetent.

clue.text: Ritualistic symbol, when mounted, satisfied the Scriptures

indicators.note: when mounted means the pieces are read upwards in this down entry

parts.note: to meet a demand is to satisfy it, so met
OT is the Old Testament, part of the Scriptures

explanation.surface: A ritual emblem, once put up, met the demands of Scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when mounted' turns MET OT upside down, to read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a natural object or carved figure revered as an emblem of a clan, used in ritual.

clue.text: A light in the bay

parts.note: reads like a lamp shining over a stretch of sea, but a light is a window set in a projecting bay of a house

explanation.definitionFit: This kind of window curves outward in a bay, and a window is a light.

clue.text: Get confused about caged bird

indicators.note: caged means the word for about is shut inside the scrambled letters
confused means the letters are mixed up

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone gets confused about a bird in a cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' scrambles the first word, and 'caged' shuts the short word for about inside that scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a kind of white heron, a wading bird.

clue.text: Arrives during race to provide voice-over

indicators.note: during says one piece occurs in the middle of the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: a race of people can be called a nation
ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrives

explanation.surface: Someone turns up mid-race to commentate over the footage.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice-over is spoken commentary over film, a narration by an unseen speaker.

clue.text: Historic fortress with the power to draw?

definitions.meaning: the ... of London, the ancient castle on the Thames
a thing that tows or pulls, read whimsically as tow plus -er

explanation.surface: A famous old castle with the strength to pull something along.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tower is London's historic fortress, and a tower in the jokey sense is a vehicle that tows.

clue.text: Animal writer loses head crossing square to bar

indicators.note: crossing means the shortened writer reaches across and holds the square inside
loses head means the writer's name drops its first letter

parts.note: Aesop, the Greek author of animal fables
a T-square is the draughtsman's square, giving T

explanation.surface: A fable writer, losing his head over a square, is barred.
explanation.walkthrough: AESOP minus its first letter is ESOP, and T goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to estop is to preclude or prevent someone from asserting something, to bar them.

clue.text: Writer's monument is in Berlin

parts.note: a column such as Nelson's is a monument
the German word for is is ist

explanation.surface: An author's memorial stands in Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Writer' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A columnist writes a regular newspaper feature, so is a writer.

clue.text: To travel over snow at first takes skill

parts.note: to sleigh is to ride over snow in a sledge

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Getting across snow takes skill at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means dexterity or cunning, as in sleight of hand, so it is skill.

clue.text: Concerning work efficiency, perhaps, or governor's initial income?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged otherwise
initial asks for the first letter of the word governor

explanation.surface: Is a governor's starting salary perhaps about getting work done efficiently?
explanation.walkthrough: OR, G and INCOME are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergonomics studies efficiency in the working environment, so this adjective relates to it.

clue.text: Trains carrying many keeping a religious fast

indicators.note: carrying means the railway holds the other letters within it

parts.note: RLY is the abbreviation for railway, which runs trains
PI is short for pious, a crossword sense of religious
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number; keeping just joins it to what follows

explanation.surface: Trains carrying crowds while observing a religious fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Railway gives the outer letters; 'fast' looks like a religious fast but is the adverb meaning quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidly means quickly, and fast as an adverb means the same.

clue.text: Urge president to provide a means of transport

parts.note: to push someone is to urge them on
a chair is the president of a meeting

explanation.surface: Encourage a president to arrange transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to provide' is a link. A pushchair is the British word for a baby's stroller.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushchair, a folding seat on wheels for a small child, carries the child about.

clue.text: The old strayed badly a short time ago

parts.note: ye is an old form of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe

indicators.note: badly means the following word's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The elderly man wandered off badly not long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles only the word strayed; the archaic 'ye' stays at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday means the day before today, and loosely the recent past.

clue.text: Sniper returns and receives pieces of gold

indicators.note: returns means the word for the sniper comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: a gun is a gunman, such as a sniper
to receive something is to get it

explanation.surface: A sniper comes back and is paid in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns GUN into NUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuggets are lumps of gold found in the ground, pieces of the precious metal.

clue.text: Cut a woman's slip

parts.note: a slit is a cut
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A tear in a lady's petticoat.
explanation.definitionFit: To slither is to slide or slip along.

clue.text: Refuses to acknowledge Isaiah's presence in the hills

indicators.note: presence in says the abbreviated prophet is found inside the hills

parts.note: the Downs are chalk hills in southern England
IS is the standard abbreviation for the Book of Isaiah

explanation.surface: Someone denies that the prophet Isaiah was ever in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The Downs are ranges of chalk hills in southern England, such as the South Downs.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to deny any connection with them, to refuse to acknowledge them.

clue.text: Poker-faced college official sheltering a displaced person

indicators.note: sheltering means the official holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a dean is a senior college official
DP is the abbreviation for displaced person, a refugee

explanation.surface: A stony-faced dean shelters a refugee.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadpan means expressionless, showing no emotion, like a card player hiding a hand.

clue.text: Pieces of bacon he carries in fine porcelain

indicators.note: pieces of means the words are broken up and their letters put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Bits of bacon are served by him on the best china.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' is a link joining the fodder BACON HE to IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone china is a fine translucent porcelain made with bone ash.

clue.text: A singer grabbed one for support

indicators.note: grabbed means the singer seizes the letter and holds it inside

parts.note: a bass is a singer with the lowest voice
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A vocalist seized someone to lean on.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is a foundation, what something rests on or is supported by.

clue.text: Stage school

definitions.meaning: to school someone is to train or tutor them

explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a stagecoach, and to coach is to train or teach someone.

clue.text: Composed type found in this hunting-land

definitions.meaning: in printing, a ... is the iron frame that holds set type
an unenclosed park kept for hunting deer

explanation.surface: A printer's set type is found on hunting grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Chase names both a printer's frame for locked-up type and a stretch of open ground for hunting.

clue.text: Help with a disguise, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: a veil hides the face, a disguise

explanation.surface: Assistance with a costume, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means use or benefit, as in to no avail, so it is help.

clue.text: An Indian city sounds almost the same without one

indicators.note: without means the letter for one is removed from what remains
almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: similar means alike or the same
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An Indian city whose name sounds nearly identical, lacking only one thing.
explanation.walkthrough: SIMILAR minus its last letter is SIMILA; taking out I leaves the city. 'sounds' is a link, nodding to how close the name is to the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Simla (now Shimla) is the hill station that served as the summer capital of British India.

clue.text: Difficult to insert first and last letters left out by chance

indicators.note: to insert says other letters are placed inside the word for difficult

parts.note: hard means difficult

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is removed from the first letter's name

parts.note: alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: It is hard to fit in the first and last letters, so some get left out at random.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' here is the Greek first letter, losing its L to 'out'; with the alphabet's last letter it goes in after the opening H of the word for difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Haphazard means random or unplanned, occurring by chance.

clue.text: Sweetener for tea given to a politician in error

indicators.note: in says the gift of tea to the politician goes inside the word for error

parts.note: a sin is a moral error or wrongdoing

indicators.note: given to means the tea is attached to what comes before it

parts.note: C is short for Conservative, a politician
char is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Something to sweeten tea is wrongly given to a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. Char is everyday British slang for tea, and 'error' is moral, a sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharin is an artificial sugar substitute, used as a sweetener in drinks.

clue.text: Broadcast about one of Macaulay's ancient Roman poems?

parts.note: re means about or concerning

parts.words: one of Macaulay's ancient Roman poems?
parts.note: Macaulay wrote the Lays of Ancient Rome, so one of them is a lay

explanation.surface: A radio piece about Macaulay's poems of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Macaulay's Lays of Ancient Rome (1842) include Horatius at the bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To relay is to pass on or transmit a signal, as in broadcasting.
